question.problem:
The function $f(x),$ defined as

$$
f(x)=\frac{2}{k\sqrt[3]{6x-1}}+2,\,x\ne \frac{1}{6}
$$

has an inverse function given by 

$$
{f}^{-1}(x)=\frac{4}{81(x-2)^{3}}+\frac{1}{6},\,x\ne 2.
$$

What is the value of $k?$

$k=$
{{field-1}}
question.worked_solution:
To find ${f}^{-1}(x),$ we start by replacing $f(x)$ with $y:$

$$
y=\frac{2}{k\sqrt[3]{6x-1}}+2
$$

Now, interchanging $x$ and $y$ gives

$$
x=\frac{2}{k\sqrt[3]{6y-1}}+2.
$$

Then, we make $y$ the subject of the equation as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =\frac{2}{k\sqrt[3]{6y-1}}+2 \\ \frac{2}{k\sqrt[3]{6y-1}} & =x-2 \\ \sqrt[3]{6y-1} & =\frac{2}{k(x-2)} \\ {(\sqrt[3]{6y-1})}^{3} & ={(\frac{2}{k(x-2)})}^{3} \\ 6y-1 & =\frac{{2}^{3}}{{k}^{3}(x-2)^{3}} \\ 6y & =\frac{8}{{k}^{3}(x-2)^{3}}+1 \\ y & =\frac{4}{3{k}^{3}(x-2)^{3}}+\frac{1}{6}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the inverse function is 

$$
{f}^{-1}(x)=\frac{4}{3{k}^{3}(x-2)^{3}}+\frac{1}{6},\,x\ne 2.
$$

Comparing our answer with the given expression, we conclude that

$$
\frac{4}{3{k}^{3}}=\frac{4}{81}\,⟹\,k=3.
$$
